channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Ten and twelve-and-a-half: the tariff wall comes back
item.description: A new Section 301 regime puts 10% duties on jewelry from India, Canada and Britain and 12.5% on China, Thailand, Turkey and the UAE, effective July 24. Diamonds polished in the EU keep their exemption.

item.title: Surat does the math on ten percent
item.description: India polishes roughly nine in ten of the world's diamonds by volume, and the United States is its largest customer. A 10% duty on Indian polished, live July 24, lands on a trade already thinned by cheap rough and soft margins.

item.title: Gold near $4,061 waits on the Fed
item.description: Gold ended the week around $4,061 an ounce, up roughly 2% on the week but still short of $4,100, as traders positioned for a Federal Reserve widely expected to hold rates when it meets July 28 and 29.

item.title: Platinum runs short a fourth year, and still slips
item.description: The World Platinum Investment Council sees a 297,000-ounce supply deficit in 2026, a fourth straight shortfall, even as spot platinum fell about 1% Friday to $1,574 and jewelry demand for the metal drops 12%.

item.title: India buys the dip as gold falls ten percent
item.description: Indian gold fell about 10% in June to a six-month low near 141,000 rupees per 10 grams, and buyers came back: listed jewellers logged 30-60% revenue growth, though old-gold trade-ins now fund up to 55% of counter sales.

item.title: List prices up, resale down: the watch gap narrows
item.description: Swiss brands raised US retail prices about 7% for 2026 while the secondary market slid roughly 8% to two-year lows, squeezing the premium that once made a steel sports watch behave like an investment.

item.title: Furmanovich cuts Art Deco from straw and beetle-wing
item.description: The Brazilian marquetry house has translated 1920s geometry into straw inlay, Shibayama, abalone and iridescent beetle-wing, a couture-level collection arguing that craft, not carat weight, is the luxury on offer.

item.title: De Beers digs 88% more, banks 44% less
item.description: Second-quarter rough output jumped 88% to 7.8 million carats even as the average price fell 32% to $105 a carat. Revenue slid 44% to $665 million. Production is rising into the weakest market in a generation.

item.title: Gold defends $4,000 as oil clears $100
item.description: Bullion held $4,028 on Friday, a whisker above the $4,000 line, as Brent crude topped $100 and the ten-year yield reached 4.70%. Traders now price an 80% chance of a September rate rise, up from 68%.

item.title: The Apollo Gallery reopens, minus the crown jewels
item.description: Nine months after thieves took over $100 million in French royal jewels in a seven-minute raid, the Louvre's Apollo Gallery reopened July 22. The jewels will not return to it. Four suspects are in custody; the stones are still gone.

item.title: Emeralds hold at $146 a carat; rubies wait their turn
item.description: Gemfields' higher-quality emerald auction took $26.8 million, selling 36 of 37 lots at an average $146.08 a carat. A 10% slide in the rupee weighed on Indian buyers, and the miner is treading carefully on rubies after a $51 million loss.

item.title: Small stones lead again as one-carat goods slip
item.description: RapNet's June index rose 4.2% for 0.30-carat diamonds and 1.3% for half-carats, while the one-carat benchmark fell 0.7%. Inventory cuts, not fresh demand, are doing the lifting at the small end.

item.title: Lab-grown now costs 73% less; naturals win the ring back
item.description: A study of appraisal data finds lab-grown diamonds priced 73% below naturals, up from a 27% gap in 2019. As the discount widened, natural stones reclaimed 57% of engagement rings, the reversal grown diamonds were supposed to prevent.

item.title: Trophies carry Sotheby's to $31.4 million; a pink walks
item.description: Sotheby's New York High Jewelry sale made $31.4 million with 95% sold, led by a $3.2 million Graff diamond ring. Down the street, Phillips withdrew a 3.03-carat fancy pink when bids missed its reserve.

item.title: Swiss watch exports jump 11.2%, but the profit doesn't follow
item.description: June's 11.2% export rebound was the strongest reading in a year and sent Swatch shares higher. Yet the group's half-year profit was CHF 16 million on CHF 3.12 billion of sales, half a percent. The volume is back; the margin is not.

item.title: Fifty percent for Canada: the wall reaches the diamond counter
item.description: A 50% tariff on Canadian goods takes effect August 19 and names six jewelry HTS codes, loose polished diamonds among them. Rough is exempt, USMCA offers no shelter, and the duty stacks on top of everything already in force.

item.title: Twelve and a half for color: Washington prices the rainbow
item.description: USTR's expedited Section 301 investigation proposes 12.5% tariffs on colored gemstones and cultured pearls from roughly 46 countries, with resolution expected by end of July. Brazil's 25% is already in force, and the temporary 10% global surcharge expires July 24.

item.title: Oil talks, gold listens: $4,165 was the top, for now
item.description: Gold backed off Wednesday's two-week peak of $4,165.87 to trade $4,103.39 Thursday morning, down 0.6%, as oil hit a six-week high, two-year yields touched a 17-month peak and futures put 77% odds on a September rate hike.

item.title: Swatch's split screen: nine percent growth, sixteen million profit
item.description: Swatch Group's first half: revenue CHF 3.12 billion, up 2% reported and 9% at constant currency, with the US up 27%, Japan up 20% and Spain up 28%. Net profit fell 6% to CHF 16 million — a margin of half a percent.

item.title: Birks trims the loss by 73 percent: a repair year in Montreal
item.description: Canada's jeweler of record cut its annual net loss to CAD 3.4 million from CAD 12.8 million, on sales of CAD 205.4 million, up 15.5%, with comparable-store sales up 2.6%. A new mono-brand store lands in Vancouver this fall.

item.title: The $21,650 lemon: Monica Rich Kosann's fruit that opens
item.description: Three pendants in the Enchanted Garden series — a cherry at $10,985, a pear at $14,500 and a lemon at $21,650 — each a hinged locket concealing garnets or diamond ‘seeds’ inside 18-karat gold and pavé.

item.title: 2,800 square feet for the crown: Tysons gets its Rolex
item.description: Liljenquist & Beckstead, family jewelers since 1978, opened a 2,800-square-foot Rolex boutique in Tysons Galleria on July 22 — bronze-brass façade, walnut walls, and a Rolex-trained watchmaking workshop built to be watched.

item.title: The $144 day: gold breaks its quiet week early
item.description: Kitco's late-Tuesday board read $4,131, up 1.33%, after a stretch that ran from $3,998.80 at the low to $4,142.70 at the high. Silver traded to $60.11, platinum added 2.28%, and the Fed is still six days out.

item.title: Seventy percent old gold: India's counter learns to recycle
item.description: The World Gold Council's July update shows imports down 42% in June to $1.97 billion, the lowest since June 2025, while some retailers report old-gold exchanges at up to 70% of jewelry sales and April-June revenue up 30-60%.

item.title: Gold up fifty, diamonds down fifty-eight: Luk Fook's split quarter
item.description: Retail sales rose 32% in April-June and gold same-store sales gained 50%, but diamond same-store sales fell 17% group-wide and 58% on the mainland. Chow Sang Sang grew 16%. Both chains kept closing stores.

item.title: ‘Disposable tools’: the miners’ union answers De Beers
item.description: The National Union of Mineworkers has condemned the two-year Venetia pause that puts 1,134 mine employees and 80 sales staff into consultation, accusing De Beers of presenting a predetermined decision and proposing cuts that start in the executive suite.

item.title: Sixty-one percent: the aisle has already voted
item.description: The Knot's 2026 Real Weddings study finds 61% of couples who married in 2025 chose lab-grown center stones. Wholesale prices fell 14-15% in the first quarter; a premium one-carat lab stone now retails for $800-$1,200.

item.title: Thirty-five percent at midnight: Brazil's rough rides free
item.description: A 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazilian goods takes effect July 23, stacking to 35% on polished stones and finished jewelry. Rough gemstones and unwrought precious metals are exempt, and the math may soon read 37.5%.

item.title: Graff pins the butterfly: twelve brooches built to tremble
item.description: A new high-jewelry capsule revives the 17th-century jabot pin with en tremblant wings, Paraíba tourmalines, invisibly set pink sapphires and a house motif dating to 1975. Every piece converts to a pendant. Prices on request.

item.title: Piaget doubles at Bonhams, and the trophy era loosens
item.description: Record spring sales saw Piaget models double and triple in value, a 1970s Cartier Bamboo Coussin bring $114,800 and a gold Polo Jumbo $33,280 — while a 1930s Rolex Prince went for $2,176. The market is widening, not just rising.
